about.heading: Engineering with intent
about.lead: I’m a software engineer who enjoys turning ideas into working products from the interface people use to the services, data, infrastructure, and systems behind them.
paragraphs: My experience spans web and mobile applications, backend and API development, databases, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, and CI/CD. I enjoy working across the different parts of a product and understanding how they fit together in production.
I care about the details that make software dependable: clear architecture, well-designed APIs, sensible data models, reliable deployments, and systems that are straightforward to maintain.
Whether I’m building a product from scratch or improving an existing system, I focus on keeping the engineering practical, the experience thoughtful, and the result ready for real users.

projects.title: What's Next
projects.description: A full-stack productivity application built across the frontend, backend, database, authentication, and deployment layers.
projects.longDescription: What's Next is a full-stack productivity application designed as a real product rather than a simple CRUD project. I built the application across the frontend, backend API, relational data layer, authentication, containerized infrastructure, and automated deployment workflow.
projects.problem: I wanted to build a complete product that covered the engineering lifecycle beyond application code, including data modeling, authentication, deployment, infrastructure, and continuous delivery.
projects.solution: Built a complete web application with a Next.js frontend, NestJS backend, PostgreSQL database, authentication, Docker-based deployment, reverse proxy configuration, and automated CI/CD.

architecture.frontend: Next.js application using the App Router.
architecture.backend: NestJS REST API organized into modular services with authentication and validation.
architecture.database: PostgreSQL with Prisma for schema management, queries, and migrations.
architecture.authentication: Supabase Auth integrated into the application.
architecture.containerization: Docker used to package and run the application services.
architecture.reverseProxy: Nginx configured as the reverse proxy in front of the backend.
architecture.ciCd: GitHub Actions builds and publishes container images to GitHub Container Registry.
architecture.deployment: Cloud-hosted deployment with Watchtower automatically pulling updated container images and restarting the application.

work: Designed and developed the frontend application.
Built the backend REST API using NestJS.
Designed the PostgreSQL data model.
Used Prisma for database schema management, queries, and migrations.
Integrated authentication.
Containerized application services using Docker.
Configured Nginx as a reverse proxy.
Created the CI/CD workflow using GitHub Actions.
Published Docker images through GitHub Container Registry.
Configured Watchtower for automated container updates.
Worked through deployment, environment configuration, database migration, and infrastructure issues.
challenges: Keeping the frontend, API, and database layers consistent as the application evolved.
Managing database schema changes and migrations.
Keeping local, CI, and production environments consistent.
Creating a repeatable deployment process without manually rebuilding the server for every release.
Managing application configuration across multiple environments.
solutions: Used Prisma for structured database schema management and migrations.
Structured the backend using NestJS modules and services.
Used Docker to provide a consistent application environment.
Automated image builds and publishing through GitHub Actions.
Used Nginx to handle reverse proxying.
Used Watchtower to automate container updates after new images were published.
highlights: End-to-end full-stack development.
Typed frontend and backend development.
Relational database architecture using PostgreSQL and Prisma.
Authentication integrated into the application.
Dockerized application deployment.
Automated CI/CD workflow.
Cloud-hosted production environment.
projects.outcome: A complete full-stack product with a repeatable development and deployment workflow spanning application code, database, authentication, containers, infrastructure, and CI/CD.

projects.title: Hungry Hub
projects.description: A college cafeteria ordering application built to simplify food ordering and management through a mobile interface.
projects.longDescription: Hungry Hub was a college cafeteria ordering application built as a mobile-first product. The project involved developing the mobile application, backend API, database integration, and the application workflow required to place and manage cafeteria orders.
projects.problem: The project was designed to make college cafeteria ordering more convenient by moving the ordering workflow into a dedicated mobile application.
projects.solution: Built a React Native mobile application backed by a Node.js and Express API with MongoDB for application data.

architecture.mobile: React Native application developed with Expo.
architecture.backend: Node.js and Express.js backend providing application APIs.
architecture.communication: Mobile application communicates with the backend through APIs.

work: Developed the mobile application using React Native and Expo.
Built backend APIs using Node.js and Express.js.
Worked with MongoDB for application data.
Connected the mobile application with backend services.
Implemented the core cafeteria ordering workflow.
challenges: Connecting the mobile application with backend services.
Designing the application workflow around cafeteria ordering.
Managing application data between the mobile client, API, and database.
solutions: Used React Native and Expo to build the mobile client.
Created a Node.js and Express.js API layer between the application and database.
Used MongoDB as the persistence layer.
Separated the mobile interface from backend application logic.
highlights: Mobile application built with React Native.
Expo-based development workflow.
Node.js and Express.js backend.
MongoDB data layer.
End-to-end mobile-to-backend integration.
projects.outcome: A complete mobile ordering application connecting a React Native client with backend APIs and a MongoDB data layer.

projects.title: Ashutosh Rath - Portfolio
projects.description: A personal engineering portfolio designed to present my work, technical capabilities, experience, and projects through an interactive web experience.
projects.longDescription: My portfolio website is a custom web experience built to represent how I approach software engineering. Rather than using a static resume-style layout, the site is designed around interactive sections, project storytelling, technical capabilities, experience, and reusable content structures.
projects.problem: I wanted a portfolio that represented the breadth of my engineering work across mobile, web, backend, cloud, infrastructure, and AI without turning the site into a simple list of technologies.
projects.solution: Built a custom portfolio experience with reusable components, structured content, responsive layouts, animations, and a data-driven approach that allows the site's content to evolve independently from its presentation.

architecture.components: Reusable UI components organized around portfolio sections and content types.
architecture.content: Portfolio content structured through JSON/schema-driven data rather than being tightly coupled to individual UI components.
architecture.animation: GSAP used for interactive transitions, scroll-driven effects, and motion.
architecture.styling: Tailwind CSS and custom design tokens used for the visual system.
architecture.responsive: Responsive layouts designed to work across desktop and mobile screen sizes.

work: Designed the overall portfolio information architecture.
Built reusable React components for portfolio sections.
Created the project presentation and case-study structure.
Built the experience timeline.
Created interactive skills and technology relationships.
Implemented scroll-based animations and transitions using GSAP.
Implemented custom cursor and interaction effects.
Designed responsive layouts for different screen sizes.
Structured portfolio content using JSON/schema-driven configuration.
Worked on accessibility and reduced-motion considerations.
designPrinciples: Content should be separated from presentation where practical.
Components should be reusable rather than duplicated across sections.
Animations should support the experience rather than interfere with usability.
The interface should remain responsive across screen sizes.
The portfolio should communicate engineering work through projects and systems rather than only through a technology list.
highlights: Custom portfolio experience rather than a template-based resume page.
Reusable React component architecture.
Schema-driven portfolio content.
GSAP-powered interactions and scroll animations.
Responsive design.
Interactive project and experience sections.
Custom visual system and interaction details.
projects.outcome: A personal engineering portfolio that presents projects, experience, capabilities, and technical work through a custom interactive web experience.

codeToCloud.heading: From code to cloud
codeToCloud.description: A practical engineering workflow that brings together application development, data, cloud infrastructure, automation, and AI.

stages.label: Build
stages.description: Develop web and mobile applications with reusable components, clear application structure, and maintainable code.

stages.label: Connect
stages.description: Build APIs and integrate frontend, backend, databases, and external services into complete application workflows.

stages.label: Model
stages.description: Design data models, write SQL, manage database schemas, and build reliable data flows that support application requirements.

stages.label: Collaborate
stages.description: Use Git-based workflows, code reviews, and engineering practices that make changes easier to understand, review, and maintain.

stages.label: Automate
stages.description: Use CI/CD pipelines and engineering tools to automate builds, quality checks, and application delivery.

stages.label: Package
stages.description: Use Docker and consistent application configuration to create reproducible environments across development and deployment.

stages.label: Deploy
stages.description: Take applications into cloud-hosted environments and work with infrastructure, networking, and deployment workflows needed to run them.

stages.label: Operate
stages.description: Support applications in production through monitoring, troubleshooting, incident investigation, root-cause analysis, and reliability improvements.

stages.label: Apply AI
stages.description: Build AI-powered capabilities and use modern AI tools to augment applications, automate workflows, and improve the software engineering process.
